title: Refusal
description: The platform's coded refusal: a sentence for a person in `detail` and, BESIDE it (never under it), a machine-readable `code`. grid-proxy sends it for a grid that is not up; a master sends it for a retired feature. The public CLI compares `code` for EQUALITY, never for truthiness and never paired with the status, and reads a code it does not know, or none, as a transient failure. grid-proxy's codeless answers have this shape too: `404 unknown network`, `503` while a wake is starting (with `Retry-After: 20`), and `502`/`504` when the master did not answer. The public CLI acts on exactly three codes (grid_asleep, grid_stopped, grid_deleted); it must never parse the others, so that renaming one of them cannot change what a provider does.

detail.description: A sentence for a person. Clients render it; its wording is not part of the contract.

code.description: The refusal's name, when it has one. Each named refusal is a definition below.

GridAsleep.description: The grid is asleep and this request did not wake it. A request that may wake a grid (a signed-in read, inference, an owner's act, a provider's registration) is held and replayed instead, unless grid-proxy's limits turn it away (then with a Retry-After: past a wake limit nothing is woken, past the waiting bound the grid IS waking and only this request is not held); a provider's heartbeat, poll and callbacks, and any credential-less read, never wake one. The public CLI's provider PARKS on it: its heartbeat probes every ASLEEP_PROBE_SECONDS, bring-up on its own schedule, and the engine serves again by itself after a wake.

last_known.description: Only on the answer to a credential-less GET of the overview, after `detail` and `code`. Absent when the platform holds no record for the grid, or none younger than LAST_KNOWN_MAX_AGE_SECONDS.

x-headers.Retry-After: Optional, whole seconds. Sent when grid-proxy's limits (grid-platform ticket 21) turned away a request that may wake the grid: past a WAKE limit (the episodes a client may start, or a grid may have, per window) nothing was asked, and it is when the oldest counted wake leaves the window, up to the window's length; past the WAITING bound (the requests waiting at once, one client's share of them, the bytes they hold) the grid is waking anyway, and it is the master's boot. Otherwise absent. A reader must work without it: the public CLI's park branches on the code alone.

GridStopped.description: The grid's OWNER stopped it, and nothing wakes it until the owner starts it: not inference, not a read, not a join. The public CLI's provider parks on it as on grid_asleep, probing every STOPPED_PROBE_SECONDS.

GridDeleted.description: The grid was deleted. The only refusal that ENDS a provider: the public CLI stops the engine for good, so a false positive would stop a provider serving a live grid. An older proxy answered `404 unknown network` with no code instead.

GridMasterDown.description: The grid should be running but its master refused the connection; the platform is bringing it back. Deliberately NOT parsed for its value by the public CLI: a parked provider leaves the park on any code other than a pause code, and otherwise retries it like any 503.

x-headers.Retry-After: `10` while the platform is restarting the master; absent otherwise.

FeatureRetired.description: The route or model name belongs to a retired feature (media, distributed tasks, effort mode), and the master answers this instead of serving it. The public CLI must not parse it.
